title: Opposite transports in a bicartesian interval fibration are adjoint
statement:
Use the canonical composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, mapping spaces and homotopies from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to\Delta^1$ be both a cartesian and a cocartesian fibration, with fibers $E_0,E_1$. Suppose $R:E_1\to E_0$ is equipped with a coherent map $h:\Delta^1\times E_1\to E$ over $\Delta^1$, whose endpoints are $R$ and the inclusion of $E_1$, and whose edge at every object of $E_1$ is $p$-cartesian. Then there exist a functor $L:E_0\to E_1$ and a coherent map $k:\Delta^1\times E_0\to E$ over $\Delta^1$, with endpoints the inclusion of $E_0$ and $L$, whose edges at objects are $p$-cocartesian. These transport functors have a coherent adjunction $L\dashv R$. Explicitly, there are coherent transformations $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{E_0}\to RL$ and $\epsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}_{E_1}$, with homotopies $R\epsilon\circ\eta R\simeq1_R$ and $\epsilon L\circ L\eta\simeq1_L$ in the corresponding coherent functor categories. The adjunct maps
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(Ly,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{E_0}(y,Rz),\qquad v\longmapsto R(v)\circ\eta_y$$
are equivalences, coherently natural in $y,z$. This conclusion includes the higher compatibility of the transformations and homotopies, rather than only triangle equations in the ordinary homotopy categories of $E_0,E_1$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.5.4 (02FN), the bicartesian-to-adjunction direction; Remark 6.2.5.3 (02FM), existence and description of transport functors; Definitions 5.2.2.4 (019N) and 5.2.2.15 (01VN), the transport witnesses; Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1), the induced adjunct equivalence. Coherent adjunction has the unit/counit and triangle meaning of Definition 6.2.1.1 (02EK). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Write $i_0:E_0\hookrightarrow E$ and $i_1:E_1\hookrightarrow E$. A simplex of $\Delta^1$ is uniquely determined by its ordered vertices. Therefore a simplex of $E$ whose vertices all lie over $i$ lies in the strict fiber $E_i$; thus these fibers are full subcategories. The definition of a cartesian or cocartesian fibration supplies a quasicategory $E$, so [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes both fibers, and the functor categories used below, quasicategories. We may use canonical composition and the homotopy category of each such functor category as provided by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. For the cartesian tests below, use the opposite construction and natural mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4). Order reversal sends $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, and the last edge $\{n-1,n\}$ to the first edge $\{0,1\}$. Thus $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an inner fibration and an edge is $p$-cartesian exactly when its opposite is $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-cocartesian. The natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{E^{\mathrm{op}}}(r,s)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_E(s,r)$ identify precomposition with an opposite edge with postcomposition by the original edge, up to the canonical composition homotopy.

source.place: Proof, the two fiber inclusions; their fullness is checked degreewise. No reflective-subcategory theorem is assumed here.

proof.text: For $x\in E_0$, choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $u_x:x\to d_x$ of $0\to1$, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; for $x\in E_1$ take $d_x=x$ and $u_x=1_x$. For $d\in E_1$, both bottom entries in the mapping square for $u_x$ are one-point spaces. The cocartesian criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_E(d_x,d)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,d)$ when $x\in E_0$. When $x\in E_1$, the same assertion follows from the identity-composition homotopy of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. These are pointwise $E_1$-reflections. Dually, for $x\in E_1$ choose a cartesian lift $v_x:c_x\to x$ with $c_x\in E_0$, and for $x\in E_0$ take $c_x=x$, $v_x=1_x$. For $c\in E_0$, the bottom mapping spaces for $v_x$ are again points. For $x\in E_1$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $v_x^{\mathrm{op}}$ in $p^{\mathrm{op}}$, testing at $c$; its bottom spaces are points, and the natural opposite mapping equivalences of step 1 identify its top map with postcomposition by $v_x$. For $x\in E_0$, use the identity-composition homotopy. This gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_E(c,c_x)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(c,x)$. These are pointwise $E_0$-coreflections. All choices have been made only over objects that exist; neither fiber is assumed nonempty.

source.place: Proof, reflection and coreflection of the two fibers, expanding Corollary 6.2.5.2 by the mapping criteria.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-reflection-assembly] to the two full inclusions and the universal arrows of step 2. Obtain $A:E\to E_1$ with $a:\mathrm{id}_E\to i_1A$ exhibiting a coherent adjunction $A\dashv i_1$, and $B:E\to E_0$ with $b:i_0B\to\mathrm{id}_E$ exhibiting $i_0\dashv B$. The node also asserts the pointwise universal precomposition property of every $a_x$ and the pointwise universal postcomposition property of every $b_x$. These properties, not any particular initially chosen lifts, are what the next step uses.

source.place: Proof, Lemma 6.2.2.23 and Proposition 6.2.2.24 and their coreflective duals.

proof.text: Set $L=Ai_0$ and $R'=Bi_1$. Restrict $a$ to $E_0$ to obtain $k:\Delta^1\times E_0\to E$, and restrict $b$ to $E_1$ to obtain $h':\Delta^1\times E_1\to E$. The endpoint values are exactly $(i_0,i_1L)$ and $(i_0R',i_1)$. Their composites with $p$ agree with interval projection on vertices and hence on every simplex, by the vertex description of $\Delta^1$ in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. To test $a_y:y\to i_1Ly$ for $y\in E_0$, use [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. For test objects in $E_1$, the bottom spaces are points and the top map is the universal equivalence from step 3. For test objects in $E_0$, the left spaces of the square are empty and the lower right space is a point, so the homotopy pullback is empty. Thus $k$ has horn-cocartesian components. To test $b_z:i_0R'z\to z$ for $z\in E_1$, apply the same cocartesian criterion to $b_z^{\mathrm{op}}$ for $p^{\mathrm{op}}:E^{\mathrm{op}}\to(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a test object $c\in E_0$, the bottom spaces are points; by the natural opposite mapping equivalences of step 1, the top map is the universal equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_E(c,i_0R'z)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(c,z)$ of step 3. For a test object $c\in E_1$, its upper left and lower left entries are empty and its lower right entry is a point. Thus $b_z^{\mathrm{op}}$ is horn-cocartesian; the explicit horn reversal in step 1 makes $b_z$ horn-cartesian. Hence $h'$ has horn-cartesian components. The empty assertions follow degreewise from the absence of a base edge $1\to0$, so no nonempty mapping-space hypothesis is hidden.

source.place: Remark 6.2.5.3, restrictions of reflection and coreflection functors; both horn edge predicates are checked rather than inferred by an uncited duality.

proof.text:
Write $u:\mathrm{id}_{E_0}\to Bi_0$, $v:i_0B\to\mathrm{id}_E$ for the unit and counit of $i_0\dashv B$, and $a:\mathrm{id}_E\to i_1A$, $w:Ai_1\to\mathrm{id}_{E_1}$ for those of $A\dashv i_1$ from step 3. Set
$$\eta'=(Ba i_0)\circ u,\qquad \epsilon'=w\circ(Av i_1).$$
Whiskering is precomposition or postcomposition of the defining simplicial maps. Compose these edges in the functor quasicategories using [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. In their homotopy categories, naturality of $v$ for $a i_0$ and of $a$ for $v i_1$ gives respectively
$$\begin{aligned}
\epsilon'L\circ L\eta'&=wAi_0\circ Av i_1Ai_0\circ Ai_0Ba i_0\circ Ai_0u
\simeq wAi_0\circ Aa i_0\circ Av i_0\circ Ai_0u\simeq1_L,\\
R'\epsilon'\circ\eta'R'&=Bi_1w\circ Bi_1Av i_1\circ Ba i_0Bi_1\circ uBi_1
\simeq Bi_1w\circ Ba i_1\circ Bv i_1\circ uBi_1\simeq1_{R'}.
\end{aligned}$$
The final cancellations are the two pairs of supplied triangle identities. The naturality squares are maps on $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ times the entire source category, obtained by evaluating the coherent transformations, so these calculations occur in the functor quasicategories. The cited spine and mapping-composition statements give representatives and triangle witnesses there. This constructs the coherent adjunction $L=Ai_0\dashv Bi_1=R'$ directly.

source.place: Proof, composition of the two inclusion adjunctions; the elementary composite unit/counit and both triangle calculations are written out (Remark 6.2.1.8).

proof.text:
Both $h'$ and the given $h$ are coherent cartesian transport witnesses for the same edge of the cartesian fibration $p$. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-transport-uniqueness] gives an equivalence $s:R'\to R$ with inverse $t:R\to R'$ and inverse homotopies. Define the transformations $\eta=(sL)\eta'$ and $\epsilon=\epsilon'(Lt)$ by composition in the functor quasicategories. The existence and coherent composition of these transformations uses [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] and [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. In the homotopy categories of these functor quasicategories, [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] and the given natural transformations give
$$\epsilon L\circ L\eta=\epsilon'L\circ LtL\circ LsL\circ L\eta'\simeq\epsilon'L\circ L\eta'\simeq1_L.$$
For the other triangle, naturality of $s$ first for $Lt$ and then for $\epsilon'$, followed by naturality of $\eta'$ for $t$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
R\epsilon\circ\eta R
&=R\epsilon'\circ RLt\circ sLR\circ\eta'R\\
&\simeq s\circ R'\epsilon'\circ R'Lt\circ\eta'R\\
&\simeq s\circ R'\epsilon'\circ\eta'R'\circ t\simeq s\circ t\simeq1_R.
\end{aligned}$$
Each naturality homotopy is obtained by applying the coherent transformation to the indicated transformation (the map on $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ and the whole source category); the face/degeneracy coherence of the cited spine node composes them. The composition node for mapping spaces then realizes these equalities by triangle witnesses in the functor quasicategories. In particular this is not a deduction of coherence from objectwise triangles in $hE_0$ or $hE_1$.

source.place: Contravariant transport identifies the right adjoint; the conjugation by the natural equivalence is written out, including both triangles.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence] to the actual transformations $\eta,\epsilon$ constructed in step 6. Its two triangle hypotheses have been verified in the functor quasicategories, so it yields the equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(Ly,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{E_0}(y,Rz)$ represented by $v\mapsto R(v)\circ\eta_y$, coherently natural in both variables. Together with $k$ from step 4 this proves every clause of the item for the specified $R$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.1.17, including the unit formula and coherent mapping-space naturality.
